Thanks — quick update from SRE side: we pushed back a tiny sample of request logs (fastretail-request-logs.txt) and a short summary: around 08:47–08:53 PT we saw a sharp uptick in client-side timeouts (our frontends enforcing 1.2s timeouts) that triggered the Redwood SDK to retry (default policy). Those retries created a burst of near-simultaneous requests in a short window.

From our preliminary view, the pattern is: short client timeout -> immediate retry -> higher concurrency -> Redwood p99 appears elevated as many requests queue up (especially for longer generation prompts). We do not have evidence of a direct code rollout on Redwood that would explain CPU or GPU issues.

Logs: fastretail-request-logs.txt
Contact: Claire and myself if you need deeper slices.

---BEGIN QUOTE---
From: Claire Hu <claire@fastretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T09:12:00Z
Subject: Observed p99 latency spike impacting checkout

Preliminary findings from infra/serving: we've pulled ingress QPS and queue-length metrics for the tenant and global clusters. Snapshot (attached) shows:
- Global cluster p99 increased ~420ms during the window; p95 up ~120ms.
- Tenant tail latency correlates to short bursts of elevated concurrency (measured as spike in in-flight requests).
- No kernel or model rollout recorded for that timeframe. No infra scale event triggered.

Hypothesis: a client-side retry/backoff pattern (aggressive retries with short client timeouts) created a transient storm that amplified queuing pressure at the ingress, which manifests as higher tail latency. This commonly gets misattributed as a Redwood platform regression.

Immediate recommendations:
1) Customer comms: explain probable cause, commit to deeper tail analysis and mitigation plan.
2) Engineering: Add tenant-aware surge protection (soft rate-limit / early-reject) + better queue-shepherding at ingress to prevent amplification.
3) SDK: Review default retry/backoff and timeout guidance — push a recommended config and a patch to change default backoff to exponential+jitter.

I'm attaching metric-snapshot-20270603.png.

Sergio Alvarez
Director, Customer Reliability (Redwood Inference)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-06-07T15:03:00Z
Subject: Executive summary + action plan for FastRetail p99 spike (for leadership)

Team — executive note to close the loop and request approval for the proposed mitigations. TL;DR: root cause is likely amplification from client-side timeouts + SDK retry behavior, not an internal model/runtime regression. Evidence: aligned timestamps, no rollout/infra event, tenant in-flight bursts during the window.

Proposed remediation and customer commitments:
- Short-term (within 24h): Notify FastRetail with clear explanation, recommended client settings (increase client timeout to >=2.5s for generation paths, disable immediate retries), and offer a one-hour on-call pairing to tune their prod SDK config.
- Mid-term (2–3 weeks): Release SDK patch that changes default retry to exponential backoff with jitter and increases default client timeout guidance; publish a migration note.
- Platform hardening (1–2 months): Implement tenant-aware surge protection (soft early-reject) and per-tenant ingress queue shaping to prevent amplification. Also add metrics to detect client-retry storms and alert earlier.

Requested approvals:
- Rishi: confirm we can prioritize SDK default change as a high-priority patch.
- Hannah/Sergio: confirm engineering bandwidth for ingress surge controls and ETA.
- Marissa: sign off on the customer comms draft and credit/compensation guidance if FastRetail requests it.

I'll draft the customer-facing note after approvals and coordinate a short cross-team incident review.

Thanks — Jonas
